raw_segments.text: Secondly, when the prince hinders the legislative from assembling in its due time, or from acting
freely, pursuant to those ends for which it was constituted, the legislative is altered.
For it is not a certain number of men, no, nor their meeting, unless they have also freedom
of debating, and leisure of perfecting, what is for the good of the society wherein the
When these are taken away or altered, so as to deprive the society of the due exercise
of their power, the legislative is truly altered.
For it is not names that constitute governments, but the use and exercise of those powers that
So that he, who takes away the freedom, or hinders the acting of the legislative in its
due seasons, in effect takes away the legislative and puts an end to the government.
